Cc: security@healthspring.com
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 13:24:00 -0700
Subject: HealthSpring: KMS/Retention questions + evidence request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team reviewed the platform and attached a short questionnaire focused on KMS/BYOK, audit-log granularity, and retention controls. A few high-level asks we need clarified before we proceed to procurement: 

- Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for both Dedicated and Private deployments? Is an HSM required or is a cloud KMS integration sufficient?
- What audit log fields are captured (actor, request id, model id, input hash, token counts)? Can these be scoped per-tenant and exported?
- Retention: can we configure short-lived retention windows for message-level logs (e.g., 30 days) and longer windows for billing metadata?
- Evidence: we need a short timeline for an evidence package (SOC2 artifact mapping, key lifecycle documentation, sample audit export).

I've attached the questionnaire (HealthSpring_SecurityQuestionnaire_v1.pdf). Can we schedule a 30-minute interlock next week to walk the asks and owners? Proposed attendees: myself, our security engineer (security@healthspring.com), and your compliance/infra owners.

Thanks,
Linda Park
Head of Security, HealthSpring

Attachments: HealthSpring_SecurityQuestionnaire_v1.pdf
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Linda Park <linda.park@healthspring.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthSpring: KMS/Retention questions + evidence request

Linda — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear asks. We're happy to interlock. 

Quick answers at a glance (we will expand on the call and in the evidence pack):
- BYOK/KMS: We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments via cloud-KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For HSM-backed keys, we can integrate with customer HSMs indirectly through supported KMS providers (bring-your-HSM is typically handled at their KMS layer). Hosted API (public) does not support CMK upload; it uses our managed key encryption and tenant separation.
- Audit logs: standard capture includes timestamp, principal (API key or user), request id, model id, full request/response hashes (input redacted by default), token counts, and backend host id. We can provide tenant-scoped exports.
- Retention: configurable at the tenant level for logs (default 90 days). Short windows (30d) are possible for pilot accounts; billing metadata retention is configurable separately.
- Evidence: we can produce a lean evidence bundle in ~7 business days (SOC2 trace mapping + key rotation docs + example export).

I've pulled in Marissa (compliance) and Priyom (infra/product ops) to own evidence and engineering clarifications respectively. Attendees we'd suggest for the interlock: Marissa (compliance), Priyom (platform/ops), Naomi (data-retention SLI) — will confirm availability. We can do Wed May 19 at 11:00am PT or Thu May 20 at 10:00am PT. Let me know what works and whether you require HSM-backed keys specifically (vs. cloud-KMS integration).

I've attached a short one-pager on our KMS integration model for context.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms-integration-one-pager.pdf

- Export process: ad-hoc CSV export vs. streaming to S3/GCS. Recommend offering both; customer prefers push-to-S3.

Deliverable: a single 'action register' CSV with columns: item, owner, due, status, notes. I'll draft the first pass and hand to Marissa for SOC mapping.

Next step: I'll draft the action-register and share for internal review by EOD May 25 so we can send the package to HealthSpring and lock the interlock meeting time.

— Priyom
